nikki: FYI running into a nasty combo in examples/edge-ts-labs — bundle works locally but fails in the edge sandbox with `TypeError: handler is not defined`. suspecting ESM/CJS interop + our overloads confusing tsc.

omar: that error usually means the platform expected a named export but the bundle produced a CJS-style default. which entry export do you have?

nikki: top-level file does `export default function handler(req) { ... }` and the worker config points to the file (no export specified). locally using node --loader ts-node/register works fine.

rui: worker sandboxes (Cloudflare/Vercel) are strict ESM. default-export wrappers produced by bundlers can end up as `exports.default =` which the runtime won't treat as the module's default. named exports are safer.

kate: also, I saw a related type oddity: our public SDK helper uses overloaded generics and VSCode picks the wrong overload so completions and inference are bad. sample type: ```ts
export function infer<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(opts: { model: string; input: T }): Promise<Out<T>>;
export function infer<T extends string | number>(opts: { model: string; input: T; streaming?: boolean }): Promise<Out<T>>;
```

nikki: yes! when caller passes a literal object the editor often infers the second overload and T collapses to `string | number`, losing object type info. DX is rough.

omar: overload order is important — TS chooses the first overload that is compatible when doing inference. put the more specific object overload first or add a final `T = any` fallback overload.

rui: but be careful: adding `T = any` defeats safety. consider splitting surface: keep strict internal types and export a thin, ergonomics-focused facade that maps to `any`/looser generic for the public helper. document it.

kate: on the bundler side, we've had success with these tsup/esbuild settings for edge artifacts: `format: 'esm'`, `platform: 'neutral'`, `target: 'es2022'`, and `esbuildOptions: (opts) => { opts.inject = []; opts.banner = ''; opts.footer = '' }`. also ensure `bundle: true` and mark any CJS deps as external.

nikki: tried that, still saw `__toESM` helper injected by esbuild in the bundle which created `exports.default` style code.

omar: `platform: 'node'` sometimes triggers different interop. if everything is ESM source, `platform: 'neutral'` + `format: 'esm'` should avoid helpers. also double-check `package.json` for `type: "module"` in the sample project — that influences the bundler and TS emit.

rui: another pragmatic change: avoid default exports for the worker entry. do `export const handler = async (req) => {}` and point the worker to `file.handler` in the worker config. This avoids ambiguity across bundlers.

kate: for types we should: 1) reorder overloads so object-generic is first; 2) provide a documented `inferLoose<T = any>` wrapper for quick prototyping; 3) add editor-completion unit tests (tiny .ts files that assert expected completions) to CI.

build-bot: CI: examples/edge-ts-labs build preview failed: worker-lint (error 1).

nikki: will try the named export patch + adjust tsconfig. speaking of tsconfig, our sample used `moduleResolution: 'Bundler'`. does switching to `NodeNext` help?

omar: `Bundler` is fine for many cases but NodeNext aligns with runtime Node ESM rules (esp. extension resolution). For edge runtimes that mimic Node ESM semantics, `moduleResolution: 'NodeNext'` + `module: 'ESNext'` tends to be more predictable. create a `tsconfig.edge.json` for samples to make the distinction explicit.

rui: also turn `skipLibCheck` off in the sample (set to false) so hidden mismatches surface early. it will slow local builds slightly but prevents weird downstream type collapses.

nikki: plan: 1) swap default -> named handler in the sample entry 2) add tsconfig.edge.json with NodeNext/ESNext and skipLibCheck = false 3) reorder overloads and add a `...Loose` facade 4) update README + add a quick checklist for edge onboarding. i'll open a small PR to examples/edge-ts-labs and tag y'all.

kate: also include a tiny rollup config example — some customers use rollup for edge bundles and its commonjs plugin behavior is different from esbuild.

omar: quick grep tip: if you see `exports.default =` or `__toESM(` in the built file, that's the interop. grep for `exports\.` to find CJS-style exports.

nikki: thanks everyone — will push the change and re-run the preview. ping @devex if CI still fails. :rocket:
